title: Soul Train Awards Return to Chicago with Star-Studded Taping
text: Soul Train Awards Return to Chicago with Star-Studded Taping The Soul Train Awards return to its hometown of Chicago after a two-year hiatus, featuring a star-studded taping at the Harris Theater and honoring icon Chaka Khan with the Classic Soul Honor. Thursday night was a homecoming for one of Chicago's cultural treasures, as the Soul Train Awards arrived in the city where the iconic show originated. The taping of the awards show brought stars to the Loop. After a two-year hiatus the Soul Train Awards have returned, and for the first time the program was taped in Chicago. The event included a star-studded purple carpet. Stars of music and culture gathered at the Harris Theater for Music and Dance in Millennium Park to celebrate the return of the Soul Train Awards.Starting in Chicago in 1971, and led by host and producer Don Cornelius, Soul Train highlighted music and dance for decades.\"It's a remarkable testament to the contribution that the city of Chicago has had on music, not just here in Chicago, but across this country and across the globe,\" Mayor Brandon Johnson said. City and state leaders were also among those attending the event, touting Soul Train's roots in Chicago.\"It's a part of the history of this amazing city. It's a part of our culture,\" said U.S. Sen. -elect Juliana Stratton.\"I'm glad we get to honor the Chicago of it all, Don Cornelius and what he brought. Soul Train affected so many artists and gave opportunities to so many artists,\" rapper Common said. As part of the awards show, Chicago native and music icon Chaka Khan has been recognized with the Classic Soul Honor, which celebrates an artist who has helped shape the sound and soul of R&B.\"I'm overwhelmed.I'm mainly doing this because of the things I helped do for other people, and that's what it's all really about,\" she said.
